texts: good. Aron Brae is typed as a village_potter with its 'potter' genus emitted; only the uniqueness carried by the definite 'the village potter' has no slot in the instruction set, and no rewrite would recover it.

mixed: cousinhood is recorded as a one-way opaque possession link, so 'is Tessa a cousin of Aron?' finds nothing - the mutual direction is not derivable, even though 'cousin' is exactly the mutual-by-meaning kind of predicate that has a two-way form available. Use the symmetric wording: "Aron Brae and Tessa Brae are cousins, and Aron Brae and Aelis Brae are cousins."

mixed: the rule captures the content and can fire, but the adjudicator ruled it defective (the required record of the quantifier word 'each' is missing) and confirmed that a universally quantified prepositional time adjunct - 'after each equinox' - has no stated routing at all, so this shape is unsupported territory. The supported form is a whenever-clause: "Whenever an equinox passes, Aron Brae makes vessels."

good. the name is one symbol reused for both mentions, the firing changes the vessels so they take the object-that-changes role, the kiln is the event's location, and 'behind Aron Brae's house' keeps its surface preposition on the kiln.

good. the postural 'lies' correctly mints no event - the seam sits at the base, the base is a part of the cliff, 'near the Cove Stair' keeps its surface preposition, and the name gets its own symbol, Name atom and kind atom.
good. the indefinite glassworks stays a specific witness rather than becoming a generic, its location in Faltern is recorded, and 'replacement lantern domes' is decomposed once to its head kind.
good. the ordering event, the village as orderer, 'new' handed to each dome individually, and 'in batches' kept as a surface oblique are all carried; nothing in the sentence is lost.

bad: two things break here. 're-fires' has no licensed form - the prefix cannot be split off into a repetition marker and there is no operator for 're-', so the verb is recorded either as a word you did not write ('fire') or as an opaque 're_fire' with the repetition lost; and a habitual clause about one specific subject ('the glassworks') has no way to carry a restricted bare-plural object, so the adjudicator ruled that no compliant parse exists at all and the claim would have to be dropped whole. Write it as a conditional with 'again' as its own word: "If a dome is damaged, the glassworks fires it again."

good. the fused harbor_warehouse gets its head genus, the containment reading keeps the warehouse as the acting participant rather than an owner, and 'spare' is distributed to each dome instead of being predicated of the group as an object.

mixed: the content is all there, but the adjudicator ruled the parse defective for leaving 'weekly' buried inside the weekly_market symbol, so nothing in the knowledge base states that the market is weekly and a question asking which market is weekly finds nothing. Your wording is not at fault; if the weekliness matters for reasoning, put it on the event instead: "Traders from Faltern and the inland farms come to the market each week."

good. it mirrors the instruction set's own market example - one running event with a start and an end for the interval, and the square as the event's location. Note that 'late morning' and 'mid-afternoon' survive only as opaque symbols, so they will not match a question phrased with plain 'morning' or 'afternoon'.

mixed: at group level the parse is right - the traders sail out, the lanterns are lit, and the two are ordered - but the adjudicator ruled it defective because the per-member rule was emitted for the traders and withheld for the lanterns, so no individual lantern's lighting is derivable. Nothing in your wording caused that; if you want each lantern reachable, make the universal explicit: "The traders sail out before each lantern is lit."
